stage2_results.local_context:
# The AI Phone Call Had a Human Helper

The human concierge test began without appropriate disclosure. But a human appeared from behind the scenes. A test involving Muse, Meta’s AI agent, became a reveal of what was really happening.

### The human backup plan

Through Muse, trained human contract workers made some calls and completed the exchanges with the people they called. In some cases, trained human contractors handled the calls and completed the interactions.

But that backup plan changed the meaning of the call.

### The hidden cost of a smooth call

The test began without properly telling people what was happening. Meta began testing human-concierge calls without appropriate disclosure. These workers did more than make the conversation smooth: employees raised concerns that users’ sensitive information could be inadvertently shared with call-center contractors when they handled calls.

This is the interesting, slightly frightening turn. Internal posts reported instances in which recipients hung up after realizing Muse was AI. Yet in the human-concierge test, human contractors handled some calls. And this was not adequately disclosed.

In response, a Meta executive admitted that starting a test in which contract workers made calls without properly telling people was a mistake. The human concierge feature was then rolled back for the time being.

AI stories usually focus on machines moving closer to people. Muse asks a different question: if humans enter AI’s backstage, can users be told? Who is speaking, and who can see the information?

## In one line

Unless both facts are explained at the start, a service of the future can quickly look like a call from a stranger.
